Sherlock Holmes is the most-adapted literary human character in movie history, with over 250 on-screen portrayals. Because a truly complete list of every single adaptation would span hundreds of titles, here is a curated list of the **most famous, highly acclaimed, and culturally significant Sherlock Holmes movies**, categorized by era and style.

---

### 1. The Modern Action Blockbusters (Robert Downey Jr. Era)
Directed by Guy Ritchie, these films reimagined Sherlock Holmes as a gritty, bohemian, bohemian action-hero while retaining his brilliant mind.
* **Sherlock Holmes (2009)** – Starring Robert Downey Jr. as Holmes and Jude Law as Dr. Watson. 
* **Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows (2011)** – Introducing Holmes' infamous arch-nemesis, Professor Moriarty (Jared Harris).
* *Note: A third film, "Sherlock Holmes 3," has been discussed for years and remains in development limbo.*

### 2. The *Enola Holmes* Spin-offs (Henry Cavill as Sherlock)
Based on Nancy Springer's book series, these Netflix original movies focus on Sherlock's younger sister, Enola, but feature a prominent, more emotionally grounded Sherlock Holmes played by Henry Cavill.
* **Enola Holmes (2020)** – Starring Millie Bobby Brown as Enola and Henry Cavill as Sherlock.
* **Enola Holmes 2 (2022)** – Enola opens her own agency and teams up with Sherlock on a major case.
* **Enola Holmes 3 (July 2026)** – The third film, featuring a plot where Sherlock is kidnapped and Enola must rescue him.

### 3. The Definitive Classics: Basil Rathbone & Nigel Bruce
From 1939 to 1946, Basil Rathbone played the quintessential Sherlock Holmes alongside Nigel Bruce as Watson in a legendary run of 14 movies. While the first two are set in the Victorian era, the later 12 modernize the setting to the 1940s (where Holmes even fights Nazis).
* **The Hound of the Baskervilles (1939)** *(Victorian setting)*
* **The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes (1939)** *(Victorian setting)*
* **Sherlock Holmes and the Voice of Terror (1942)**
* **Sherlock Holmes and the Secret Weapon (1942)**
* **Sherlock Holmes in Washington (1943)**
* **Sherlock Holmes Faces Death (1943)**
* **The Spider Woman (1944)**
* **The Scarlet Claw (1944)**
* **The Pearl of Death (1944)**
* **The House of Fear (1945)**
* **The Woman in Green (1945)**
* **Pursuit to Algiers (1945)**
* **Terror by Night (1946)**
* **Dressed to Kill (1946)**

### 4. Acclaimed Standalone & Retro Films
Many legendary actors have taken on the deerstalker hat in critically acclaimed, one-off theatrical movies.
* **The Hound of the Baskervilles (1959)** – A Hammer Horror adaptation starring Peter Cushing as Holmes and Christopher Lee as Sir Henry Baskerville.
* **A Study in Terror (1965)** – Starring John Neville as Holmes, who goes head-to-head with Jack the Ripper.
* **The Private Life of Sherlock Holmes (1970)** – Directed by Billy Wilder and starring Robert Stephens. A highly respected, melancholic look at the man behind the myth.
* **The Seven-Per-Cent Solution (1976)** – Nicol Williamson plays Holmes, who travels to Vienna to be treated for cocaine addiction by Sigmund Freud (Alan Arkin).
* **Murder by Decree (1979)** – Christopher Plummer plays Holmes (and James Mason plays Watson) in another, highly praised investigation into the Jack the Ripper murders.
* **Young Sherlock Holmes (1985)** – Produced by Steven Spielberg, this fantasy-adventure imagines a teenage Holmes and Watson meeting at boarding school.
* **Mr. Holmes (2015)** – Starring Ian McKellen as a 93-year-old, retired Sherlock Holmes struggling with dementia while trying to remember his final unsolved case.

### 5. Comedy, Parody & Animated Adaptations
Holmes has also been the subject of several notable parodies and family films.
* **The Great Mouse Detective (1986)** – Disney’s beloved animated film featuring "Basil of Baker Street," a heroic mouse who lives under Sherlock Holmes' residence.
* **Without a Clue (1988)** – A hilarious comedy starring Michael Caine as a dim-witted actor hired by the true genius, Dr. John Watson (Ben Kingsley), to pretend to be "Sherlock Holmes."
* **Sherlock Gnomes (2018)** – A 3D animated comedy starring Johnny Depp as the voice of a literal garden gnome detective.
* **Holmes & Watson (2018)** – A slapstick comedy starring Will Ferrell and John C. Reilly.

---

### Honorable Mentions: Iconic TV Movies & Series
If you run out of theatrical movies, several television adaptations are widely considered among the absolute best versions of the character:
* **The Jeremy Brett Series (1984–1994)** – Produced by Granada TV, Jeremy Brett’s portrayal of Holmes across several TV movies and series is widely regarded by purists as the most book-accurate version ever filmed.
* **Sherlock (2010–2017)** – The massively popular BBC series starring Benedict Cumberbatch and Martin Freeman, which modernized the detective in 21st-century London.
* **Elementary (2012–2019)** – A CBS procedural set in modern New York, starring Jonny Lee Miller as a recovering addict Sherlock Holmes and Lucy Liu as Dr. Joan Watson.
* **Young Sherlock (2026)** – A Prime Video series directed by Guy Ritchie and starring Hero Fiennes Tiffin as a 19-year-old, rebellious Sherlock solving his very first murder at Oxford.
